status: PROPOSAL. Nothing here has been checked against the venue, the rental house's datasheets or a load calculation.

provenance.fixtureList: The rental house's list as passed to Claude by the owner on 2026-09-27 (18x UP-B380F, 12x UP-250BSW, 8x UP-HK1915, 50x UP-PL5403, 2x UP-LA40WF, CO2 x6, cold spark x4, smoke x4). The codes are the rental house's internal names, not maker models.
provenance.optics: CLASS ESTIMATES, not datasheet values: the typical beam angle for each fixture class as published across makers' datasheets for that class. The real value for each code is OWED from the rental house.
provenance.positions: Placed by rule against the hall's structural grid (scripts/place/hall.py -> hall.json), so they move when the hall is rebuilt with measured dimensions.
provenance.hall: scripts/place/rigs/moxir-hall-dims-2026-09-27.json (grid and heights estimated from photographs with VGGT + perspective, snapped to GOST 23838-89) + moxir-hall-features-2026-09-27.json (gates, aisles, cranes; sizes GUESSES).

assumptions: The stage stands at the FAR end of the nave, in front of the far-end gate; the audience enters by the big gate at the other end. Decided for this model on 2026-09-27, not confirmed with the venue or the production — an ASSUMPTION. Change stage.end and re-run.
The stage is 16 m wide, 10 m deep, a 1.2 m deck, its back edge 1 m off the end wall. Guesses.

The stage truss is a ground-supported goalpost (two towers standing on the floor either side of the stage + a header) 18 m wide with its header at 6 m, 4 m in from the back of the stage. A guess at a common rental size; no truss is on the list — it is OWED.

UP-PL5403 x50 is read as 50 in total: 42 uplights (one at the base of every column — 32 in the measured 15-bay hall — and a second on the columns nearest the stage until 42 are used) and 8 on the crane bridge parked nearest the stage. If the 8 on the crane are IN ADDITION to the 50, the total becomes 58.

Lasers hang at the top of the truss towers (6 m) and are aimed UP into the roof over the audience; the rig script refuses any laser aim that descends, and any that passes under 3 m above the floor. This is a picture of intent, not a laser safety assessment — a qualified laser safety officer and the national rules (e.g. the Maximum Permissible Exposure limits of IEC 60825-1) are OWED before any 40 W laser is switched on in front of people.

The look (colours, intensities) is one static state for previsualisation, not a show. di.iiii renders a lamp as a spot light plus a translucent cone; brightness is tuned by eye for the browser, not photometrically.
CO2, cold spark and smoke are marker objects only: where they stand, nothing about what they do.

beam380.beamAngleNote: class estimate — 380 W beams are typically sold at 2-4 deg; datasheet OWED

bsw250.class: 250 W beam/spot/wash hybrid moving head, used here in spot
bsw250.beamAngleNote: class estimate — spot mode of a 250 W BSW is typically 12-18 deg; datasheet OWED

beeEye.class: 19 x 15 W RGBW bee-eye (K-series style) moving head
beeEye.beamAngleNote: class estimate — bee-eyes zoom roughly 4-50 deg; drawn at a tight 9 deg, as used for beam effects; datasheet OWED

par.beamAngleNote: class estimate — 54 x 3 W PARs ship with 25 or 45 deg lenses; drawn at 25; datasheet OWED

laser.beamAngleNote: drawn as the narrowest spot di.iiii renders (its cone clamps at 0.57 deg half-angle); a real laser beam is millimetres wide and scanned into shapes, which is not represented; datasheet OWED

groups.note: 8 beams on the stage back line, fanned up into the trusses over the dance floor
10 beams on the floor at column bases down both sides, aimed up into the roof trusses
12 on the stage truss header, alternately onto the stage floor and the back wall
8 bee-eyes on the stage floor at the front edge, aimed out and up over the audience
one at every column base, then a second on the columns nearest the stage, 42 in all
8 on the yellow crane bridge parked nearest the stage, washing the floor under it
2 lasers at the top of the truss towers, aimed up into the roof — never into the audience plane

budget.why: A browser cannot run ~90 real three.js spot lights: each is a term in the shader of every lit pixel and, with shadows on, a shadow render and a texture unit each (WebGL gives 16-32; past that every lit material fails to compile). Every fixture draws its beam cone; only these 8 lamps also light the room, and shadows are OFF by default (the owner found the first version too laggy, 2026-09-27). Measured — see scripts/place/README.md, 'The rig'.

night.note: A dim, cool night: the hall stays readable so the rig can be judged against it. Tuned by eye in the browser, not a photometric night.
